labels: Same rule as version 1: a check is expected when the protection it names is absent from the response or present in a form browsers ignore. Thirty cases were written by Gemini; Claude checked every label against browser behaviour, corrected three that described this adapter's parser instead (now in subset 'browser-parsing'), and added six more to that subset. 'browser-parsing' covers values whose effect depends on how browsers split or parse the header; each such case cites its source in 'basis'. HTTPS-only checks are out of scope: every case is plain HTTP on loopback.

cases.description: Two CSP headers: first defines default-src, second defines frame-ancestors 'none'.
Two CSP headers: first has frame-ancestors https://trusted.example.com, second has frame-ancestors *.
cases.basis: CSP headers intersect policies: the stricter policy (trusted.example.com) restricts framing even if the other policy allows all.

cases.description: CSP frame-ancestors 'self' explicitly restricts framing to the origin.
CSP frame-ancestors allows all http: schemes.
cases.basis: frame-ancestors http: allows embedding by arbitrary web origins over HTTP.

cases.description: CSP frame-ancestors allows all https: schemes.
cases.basis: frame-ancestors https: allows embedding by arbitrary secure web origins.

cases.description: CSP frame-ancestors allows *:* allowing all origins and ports.
cases.basis: frame-ancestors *:* allows embedding by any host on any port.

cases.description: Content-Security-Policy contains only whitespace and semicolons.
cases.basis: A policy consisting only of semicolons defines no directives and restricts nothing.

cases.description: CSP specifies frame-ancestors directive with no source expressions.
cases.basis: Under CSP Level 3, an empty frame-ancestors directive matches no origins (equivalent to 'none'), restricting framing.

cases.description: X-Frame-Options specifies both DENY and SAMEORIGIN in comma-separated list.
cases.basis: Browsers treat conflicting recognized X-Frame-Options tokens as fail-closed (denying framing).

cases.description: X-Frame-Options uses obsolete ALLOW-FROM URI directive without CSP.
cases.basis: ALLOW-FROM is obsolete and ignored by modern browsers; without CSP framing is unrestricted.

cases.description: X-Frame-Options specifies SAMEORIGIN repeatedly across headers.
X-Frame-Options has multiple unrecognized tokens.
cases.basis: Multiple unrecognized tokens do not match any recognized XFO directive and allow framing.

cases.description: X-Frame-Options DENY is present, but CSP frame-ancestors * overrides it per spec.
cases.basis: When frame-ancestors is present in CSP, user agents ignore X-Frame-Options. frame-ancestors * permits all framing.

cases.description: X-Content-Type-Options carries quoted 'nosniff'.
cases.basis: X-Content-Type-Options must be the unquoted token nosniff; quoted strings are not parsed as nosniff.

cases.description: Referrer-Policy has quoted token 'no-referrer'.
cases.basis: W3C Referrer Policy tokens are unquoted identifiers; quotes are not stripped and cause token mismatch.

cases.description: Referrer-Policy contains legacy meta token 'never'.
cases.basis: The token 'never' was only in legacy meta tag drafts; HTTP Referrer-Policy requires 'no-referrer'.

cases.description: Referrer-Policy specifies comma-separated valid tokens with fallback.
Referrer-Policy uses strict-origin.
Three Set-Cookie headers all include HttpOnly.
Three Set-Cookie headers; the middle one omits HttpOnly.
Set-Cookie has cookie name or value containing httponly, but no HttpOnly attribute.
cases.basis: The attribute HttpOnly must appear as a separate directive; 'foo=httponly' sets the cookie value, not the security flag.

cases.description: No security headers at all and one cookie without HttpOnly.
CSP frame-ancestors http://* with X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN.
cases.basis: CSP frame-ancestors overrides X-Frame-Options; http://* permits framing by arbitrary HTTP web hosts.

cases.description: CSP frame-ancestors https://* with X-Frame-Options DENY.
cases.basis: CSP frame-ancestors overrides X-Frame-Options; https://* permits framing by arbitrary HTTPS web hosts.

cases.description: X-Content-Type-Options has trailing semicolon 'nosniff;'.
cases.basis: Fetch specification expects exact token match 'nosniff'; trailing semicolon is invalid.

cases.description: Referrer-Policy has common typo 'origin-when-crossorigin' (missing hyphen).
cases.basis: W3C token is 'origin-when-cross-origin'; without the second hyphen the token is unrecognized and ignored.

cases.description: CSP has multiple directives (script-src, style-src, frame-ancestors 'none') where frame-ancestors is third.
X-Content-Type-Options has duplicate nosniff in a single comma-separated header.
cases.basis: Fetch standard, 'determine nosniff': the header values are joined and split on commas, and only the first value is compared with nosniff. The first value here is nosniff, so sniffing is disabled.

cases.description: Set-Cookie has no '=' separator.
cases.basis: RFC 6265bis section 5.6: a cookie string with no '=' is stored with an empty name and the string as its value. It is set, and it has no HttpOnly.

cases.description: Two Set-Cookie headers: the first has HttpOnly, the second has an empty name and no HttpOnly.
cases.basis: RFC 6265bis section 5.6: an empty name with a non-empty value is stored. The second cookie is set without HttpOnly.

cases.description: nosniff is the first of two comma-separated values.
cases.basis: Fetch standard, 'determine nosniff': the header values are joined and split on commas, and only the first value is compared with nosniff. The first value is nosniff.

cases.description: nosniff is the second of two comma-separated values.
cases.basis: Fetch standard, 'determine nosniff': the header values are joined and split on commas, and only the first value is compared with nosniff. The first value is not nosniff, so sniffing is not disabled.

cases.description: Two X-Content-Type-Options headers: an unrecognised value, then nosniff.
cases.basis: Fetch standard, 'determine nosniff': the header values are joined and split on commas, and only the first value is compared with nosniff. Two headers join in order, so the first value is not nosniff.

cases.description: A cookie whose name contains brackets, as array-style cookies do, without HttpOnly.
cases.basis: RFC 6265bis section 5.6: the name is everything before the first '='; brackets are stored as given. The cookie is set without HttpOnly.

cases.description: A cookie whose value is a small JSON object, without HttpOnly.
cases.basis: RFC 6265bis section 5.6: the value is everything up to the first ';'; braces and quotes are stored as given. The cookie is set without HttpOnly.

cases.description: A cookie followed by an attribute no browser defines, without HttpOnly.
cases.basis: RFC 6265bis section 5.6: an unrecognised attribute is ignored and the cookie is still stored. It has no HttpOnly.
